requested_parts: Whether Range 1 may target the Presence land itself as well as adjacent land.
answers.answer: Yes. Range is a maximum distance: a land at Range 0 from your Presence is within Range 1, so both the Presence land and the adjacent land are in range (subject to other restrictions).

evidence.text: - The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.

A land is not adjacent to itself, so cannot Gather/Push to itself. It is at Range 0 of itself and hence within any greater Range. An unrestricted “Move” can move a piece to its current land and counts as movement, unlike Gather/Push, which require adjacency.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Range 1 includes both Range 0 land and adjacent land.

requested_parts: Whether previously granted Powerstorm Repeat can select and use a card played later that turn.
answers.answer: Yes. Powerstorm’s once-this-turn permission may select a card played later that turn while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. The newly played Major is therefore eligible for the earlier Repeat permission after Bringer uses it normally.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: May be selected for earlier Repeat permission if still in play and otherwise eligible.

requested_parts: Whether any general per-land stack limit prevents Build/Gather/Presence placement.
Default cap for each named type.
answers.answer: No general stacking limit prevents an otherwise legal placement or Build. The summary states no standard stacking limit applies to pieces in a land, and Presence, Invaders, and Dahan are not otherwise capped per land; each type is limited by its own supply/disk rules as specified.

evidence.text: Invaders and Dahan are not limited by the supplied pieces; use substitutes or Energy markers to mark multiples if necessary. No standard stacking limit applies to pieces in a land. Presence is limited to your disks; destroyed disks are separate from unused track disks. [CORE pp.13,15–16; FAQ .9v5ka9f]

clause_coverage_check.ruling: No default per-land cap for Invaders, Dahan, or Presence.

requested_parts: When Call on Midnight’s Dream “or” branch is chosen.
Whether first option may be inspected before choosing second.
answers.answer: Choose the branch before resolving either option. Bringer cannot draw and inspect the four Major cards first and then switch to the 2 Fear option.

evidence.text: - You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]

requested_parts: Order of individual Growth, normal Energy, and play/pay.
Whether Energy/play may precede Growth.
Whether newly uncovered Energy number applies this phase.
answers.answer: The order is Growth, Gain Energy, then Play/Pay. The Spirit must finish Growth before normal Energy income or playing/paying cards. Normal income uses the highest uncovered Energy number after Growth, so a number uncovered by Growth applies this same phase.

evidence.text: Each turn follows **Spirit Phase → Fast Power Phase → Invader Phase → Slow Power Phase → Time Passes**. Finish a phase before beginning the next. Players choose the order of Powers within the appropriate Power Phase, completing one before the next. All players act simultaneously within a phase and may discuss freely. Each Spirit must finish its own Growth → Gain Energy → Play/Pay in that order, but may wait to see another Spirit's Growth or draws before making choices. **Every Spirit must finish the entire Spirit Phase before any Fast Power resolves.**

**Gain Energy:** Take Energy equal to the **highest uncovered number** on your Energy/Turn track. Energy/Turn and Card Plays each use their own **highest uncovered value**; neither track adds its uncovered numbers together. Unspent Energy carries over between turns; it is individual and cannot ordinarily be transferred to another Spirit.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Cannot take normal income or play/pay before Growth finishes.
Use new highest uncovered number in same phase.

requested_parts: Whether island Presence can be repositioned under Add Presence while track disks remain.
answers.answer: Yes. An Add Presence instruction may reposition any of the Spirit’s island Presence even if track disks remain; it is not limited to when tracks are empty.

evidence.text: - **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

requested_parts: Dread Apparitions treatment of printed Power Fear and ordinary Town destruction Fear.
Defend amount from later Power Fear.
Whether Bringer’s To Dream Fear counts and its Defend amount.
answers.answer: Dread Apparitions counts Power-generated Fear in its target land, not the normal 1 Fear for Town destruction. Thus the later ordinary Power’s printed 1 Fear adds Defend 1; its Town-destruction Fear adds none. Bringer’s 2 Fear from To Dream a Thousand Deaths is Power-generated Fear and adds Defend 2.

evidence.text: - **Dread Apparitions Fear sources:** While its effect is active, Power-generated Fear in its target land adds **Defend 1 per Fear**. Fear from **To Dream a Thousand Deaths** counts; normal Fear for destroying Towns/Cities does not, even when a Power caused the destruction. [Original core card text]

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Power-generated Fear counts; normal building destruction Fear does not.

requested_parts: Whether Ocean can choose a nonadjacent Coastal land instead of Drowning Tidal Boon’s Dahan.
Who chooses and whether optional.
answers.answer: Yes. When Ocean uses Tidal Boon, Ocean may move a Dahan pushed into its Ocean to any Coastal land, including nonadjacent. Ocean chooses whether and where; this alternative is optional.

evidence.text: - **Spirit-targeting Powers:** When the target Spirit selects “one of their lands,” it chooses the land and does as much there as possible, even if another of its lands would permit more instructions. Thus **Mantle of Dread** may Push an Explorer from a land without a Town, and **Tidal Boon** may Push Dahan from a land without a Town. Tidal Boon's “if Dahan are pushed” clause applies only to that Power's own Push. When Ocean uses Tidal Boon, Ocean may move Dahan pushed to its Ocean by that use to **any Coastal land**, including a nonadjacent one, instead of Drowning them. Ocean chooses; this alternative is optional. [Original core card text] Spirit-targeting Fear without a specified land has no particular land for **Dread Apparitions**. [Core: .9v5kfhb, .7w4gdab, .bu6oebp, where-do-spirit-targeting-powers-add-their-fear]

requested_parts: Order of Wrap in Wings First Gather and base Move.
Whether Dissolve threshold Damage precedes Explorer Push.
answers.answer: Wrap in Wings’ “First” instruction gathers up to 3 Dahan before its base Move, so gathered Dahan can then move and enable destination Defend. Dissolve’s threshold likewise makes the Invaders damage each other simultaneously before the Explorer Push.

evidence.text: - Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.

- **Core Power specifics:** **Song of Sanctity** is Slow, despite missing cost-circle ink in some printings. Its Explorer condition selects its effect: with Explorers, Push all of them; otherwise remove 1 Blight. This is not a free choice to remove Blight while Explorers remain. **Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship** line 3 Pushes all Explorers **to as many different lands as possible**, using every available legal destination up to the number of Explorers; its Invaders damaging each other do so simultaneously, **before** the Explorer Push as the threshold specifies. **Poisoned Land**'s threshold counts the Blight that its own earlier instruction added. **Tsunami**'s threshold adds Fear for each other Coastal land it affects. [Core: .7w4g9dg, .9v5kc31, .7w4ganc, .7w4g8q3, .7w4g8pc]

requested_parts: Five ordinary turn phases in order.
Whether Fast can begin before every Spirit finishes Spirit Phase.
Whether Fast Powers follow player order.
answers.answer: The phases are Spirit → Fast Power → Invader → Slow Power → Time Passes. Every Spirit must finish the entire Spirit Phase before any Fast Power resolves. Players choose the order of Powers within the Fast phase; they need not follow player order.

evidence.text: Each turn follows **Spirit Phase → Fast Power Phase → Invader Phase → Slow Power Phase → Time Passes**. Finish a phase before beginning the next. Players choose the order of Powers within the appropriate Power Phase, completing one before the next. All players act simultaneously within a phase and may discuss freely. Each Spirit must finish its own Growth → Gain Energy → Play/Pay in that order, but may wait to see another Spirit's Growth or draws before making choices. **Every Spirit must finish the entire Spirit Phase before any Fast Power resolves.**

Use Fast Power Cards in play and eligible Fast Innates. Players choose their order; finish one Power before starting another. A Power cannot interrupt another Power. You may forego a Power entirely, retaining a played card's Elements but receiving no Energy refund. A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow: use it now or forego it.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: No Fast until all Spirits finish Spirit Phase.

requested_parts: Placement of remaining Presence after setup.
Whether leftmost solid-circle Energy/Card Plays spaces are covered.
answers.answer: Put remaining Presence disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks. Leave the leftmost solid starting spaces uncovered.

evidence.text: 6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Remaining disks go on dashed spaces of both tracks.
